blocks.h2: What Does an Ejector Pump Do?
blocks.body: An ejector pump sits in a sealed basin below the basement floor. Fixtures that are lower than the sewer line, like a basement toilet, shower, laundry or wet bar, drain into the basin. When it fills, the pump lifts the wastewater up to the main sewer line. In a home with an [overhead sewer system](/elgin/overhead-sewer-systems), the whole basement drains to the basin, so the pump has an even bigger job.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber working on the discharge pipe of a basement sump pump

blocks.h2: Signs Your Ejector Pump Needs Help
blocks.intro: Stop using basement fixtures and call if:

tiles.body: The basin is filling faster than the pump can empty it.
The lid seal or the vent isn't doing its job.

tiles.h3: Basement Fixtures Drain Slowly or Back Up
tiles.body: The pump, float or check valve has failed.
A stuck float or bad check valve.

blocks.intro: We see ejector pumps in Elgin homes of every age.

items.body: Many 1990s and 2000s homes on the west side were built with a basement bathroom or a rough-in for one. Their original pumps are now due.

Homes converted after storm backups depend on the ejector for every basement drain.

blocks.h2: Ejector Pump Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: Do I have an ejector pump?
items.preview: If you have basement plumbing below the sewer line, look for a sealed basin.
items.answer: If your basement has a toilet, shower, laundry or bar sink, look for a sealed lid in the floor with pipes and a vent coming out of it. That's the ejector basin.

items.q: What do I do when the ejector alarm goes off?
items.preview: Stop using basement fixtures and call.
items.answer: Stop using every fixture that drains to the basin, including the washing machine, and keep the lid sealed. Then call us.

items.q: How long does an ejector pump last?
items.answer: Many last somewhere between 7 and 10 years or more. Wipes and grease shorten that.

items.q: Can I flush wipes with an ejector pump?
items.answer: No. Even flushable wipes wrap around the impeller and clog the pump. Only toilet paper should go down a toilet that drains to an ejector.

items.q: Can an ejector pump be added to my basement for a new bathroom?
items.preview: Yes. We install the basin, pump and venting.
items.answer: Yes. We install the sealed basin, a pump sized for the fixtures and the venting it needs, then connect it to your main line.

items.q: How much does ejector pump replacement cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on the pump and basin. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, the basin, the check valve and venting and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
